paper.title_en: High-Energy Neutrinos from Black Hole Evaporation in Neutron Stars
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the production of high-energy neutrinos from microscopic black holes formed through the gravitational collapse of asymmetric dark matter accumulated inside neutron stars. When Hawking evaporation dominates over accretion, long-lived, feebly interacting particles beyond the Standard Model escape the neutron star and subsequently decay into high-energy neutrinos. We analyze the repeated cycle of dark matter capture, black hole formation, and evaporation, identifying two distinct regimes determined by the competition between the dark matter thermalization time and the collapse cycle. In particular, we identify a partially thermalized regime in which the dark matter cloud evolves toward a quasi-stationary state with a temperature significantly exceeding that of the neutron star core. We derive the time-integrated Hawking emission, the resulting secondary neutrino spectra, and the expected Galactic and diffuse extragalactic neutrino fluxes. The predicted signal exhibits two distinctive signatures: a broad neutrino spectrum with a characteristic energy scale set by the initial Hawking temperature of the evaporating black hole, whose spectral peak naturally lies above $\mathcal{O}(10)$ TeV, and an extended Galactic component strongly concentrated toward the Galactic Center. Although the predicted event rates are generally small, the resulting signal may contribute at the percent level to the observed Galactic high-energy neutrino flux under favorable microscopic and astrophysical conditions. The proposed mechanism provides a new observational window on Hawking evaporation through microscopic black holes continuously produced inside neutron stars, linking dark matter, compact objects, black hole thermodynamics and high-energy neutrino astronomy.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 该论文提出了一个新颖的机制，通过中子星内部微观黑洞的霍金蒸发产生高能中微子，将暗物质、致密天体、黑洞热力学与高能中微子天文学联系起来，具有理论深度和新颖性。
decision.title_zh: 中子星内黑洞蒸发产生的高能中微子
decision.abstract_zh: 我们研究了通过中子星内部积累的非对称暗物质引力坍缩形成的微观黑洞产生高能中微子的过程。当霍金蒸发主导吸积时，超出标准模型的、长寿命的、弱相互作用的粒子逃逸出中子星，随后衰变成高能中微子。我们分析了暗物质俘获、黑洞形成和蒸发的重复循环，识别出由暗物质热化时间与坍缩循环之间的竞争决定的两种不同状态。特别地，我们识别出一种部分热化状态，其中暗物质云演化为准稳态，其温度显著超过中子星核心的温度。我们推导了时间积分的霍金发射、产生的次级中微子谱，以及预期的银河系和弥漫河外中微子通量。预测的信号表现出两个显著特征：一个宽的中微子谱，其特征能量尺度由蒸发黑洞的初始霍金温度设定，其谱峰自然位于$\mathcal{O}(10)$ TeV以上；以及一个强烈集中在银河系中心的扩展的银道面分量。尽管预测的事件率通常很小，但在有利的微观和天体物理条件下，产生的信号可能对观测到的银河系高能中微子通量贡献百分之一水平的量级。所提出的机制为通过中子星内部持续产生的微观黑洞观察霍金蒸发提供了一个新的观测窗口，将暗物质、致密天体、黑洞热力学和高能中微子天文学联系起来。
